title: Quenched Sichuan Sausage Bao
description: A weeknight-friendly, low-calorie Chinese dish featuring poached sausage, vegetables, and steamed bun. Perfect for a quick and satisfying dinner.

ingredients.name: Sausages (such as Chinese chorizo or Korean chorizo)

instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together sugar, light soy sauce, rice vinegar, and chili bean paste in a small bowl. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and create a whirlpool. Poach the sausages in the water for 5 minutes. Remove the sausages and set aside.
In a large skillet or wok, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the poached sausages to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, until browned. Remove the sausages and set aside.
Add the green onions to the skillet and cook for 1 minute, until softened.
Add the sugar and soy sauce mixture to the skillet and stir to combine. Cook for 1-2 minutes, until the mixture is bubbly and slightly thickened.

To assemble the bao, place a piece of dough on a flat surface and use your hands to shape it into a ball. Flatten the ball slightly into a disk shape. Place a sausage on the disk, then spoon some of the sauce over the sausage. Fold the dough over the filling to form a bun, and press the edges together to seal the bao.
Steam the bao over boiling water for 5-7 minutes, until the dough is cooked through and fluffy.
Serve the bao hot, garnished with scallions and sesame seeds.
